entries.proposition: Design: retrospective chart review of children with drug-resistant epilepsy treated with IVIG for at least a year, autoimmune epilepsy excluded.
entries.snippet: We performed a retrospective chart review of children with DRE treated with IVIG for at least 1 year within neurology clinics at the Alberta Children’s Hospital.

experimental_context.system: children 2-18 years with drug-resistant epilepsy treated with IVIG at one tertiary centre (n = 60 after exclusions), retrospective chart review, seizure frequency score at baseline, 3 and 12 months
experimental_context.endpoint: seizure frequency category (0-8 ordinal scale), at least 50 percent reduction, adverse effects

entries.proposition: Dosing and frequency were set case by case by the treating neurologist and adjusted by seizure score, with interval shortening when seizures continued.
entries.snippet: IVIG dose and frequency was determined on a case-by-case basis by the treating neurologist.

entries.proposition: Outcome is a seizure-frequency category score read from patient dashboards; analysis by repeated-measures ANOVA across three time points.
entries.snippet: The Repeated Measures ANOVA was used to detect statistical differences between independent variables (including etiology, seizure type and ASM use) and dependent variables (i.e., seizure frequency) across three time points.

entries.proposition: Overall: 36.7 percent (22 of 60) had at least a 50 percent reduction and eight of those became seizure free (13.3 percent of the cohort).
entries.snippet: Overall, 36.7% (n = 22) of patients exhibited a seizure frequency reduction by at least 50% within 1 year of IVIG use and 36.4% (n = 8) of these patients achieved seizure freedom (13.3% of the total population).

entries.snippet: After 1 year of IVIG therapy, there was a significant reduction in seizure frequencies among patients with generalized seizure types (p = 0.019) (Figure 2B).

entries.snippet: A significant reduction in seizure frequency at the one-year time point compared to baseline was observed among the group with stable or reduced ASM regimens (p = 0.045) (Figure 2D).

entries.snippet: Although our data are encouraging, our study is not without limitations inherent to retrospective designs such as the lack of randomization, absence of control group, and limited control over certain variables.

entries.proposition: Conclusion states IVIG is a safe adjuvant therapy that 'should be considered early' in refractory childhood epilepsy, particularly with genetic or unknown aetiology, though the genetic subgroup showed no significant change over time.
entries.snippet: In summary, IVIG therapy is a safe adjuvant therapy and should be considered early in children with refractory epilepsy, particularly among patients with genetic or unknown etiologies and among patients exhibiting generalized seizures.
